title: Conditions of Counsel on Signing Equity Held Under Membership and Patronage Equity Over to Another Party
content:
Equity is signed over only on classes the catalogue allows it on, only to a transferee of a class the catalogue lists, and only on a signed transfer instruction the equity desk has registered.

**Board approval.** Where the class requires board approval, the transfer is not recorded until the board has approved it, and the desk registers the application and tells the member when the board next sits rather than predicting the answer.

**Who may receive it.** The transferee must already be a member of the cooperative or must open a membership as part of the transfer, because equity cannot be held by a stranger to the cooperative.

**What a transfer does to the account.** Transferring the whole of a membership closes the transferor's account, and transferring part leaves it open with the remainder.

**What may not be done with equity.** Equity may not be pledged, sold to a third party for value, or used as security for a loan, and a member asking for any of those is passed to the equity desk of the cooperative's counsel rather than answered here.

**The class figures.** Whether the class admits a transfer at all, whether the board must approve it, the transferees the class lists and the class's transfer fee are the figures the class carries.

## The authority for the registered instruction

Whether a signed instruction stands registered is read from the cooperative's own register of equity applications before anything moves: the application must stand as an equity transfer application, registered and signed by the member, and it is identified by its own reference so that the instruction read is the instruction the transfer is being recorded on.

## A clause of these conditions no longer in force

This sentence is **no longer in force** and is set down only so that no reader applies it: "A transfer moves equity at its face value with no discount, carries the class's transfer fee, and does not reset the allocation years behind the equity, so the transferee inherits the transferor's place in the revolvement cycle rather than starting afresh." What is now counted into the equity that moves, and what is taken off it, are governed by the current basis, which is carried with the transfer valuation rules. The conditions above, on permitted classes, on listed transferees, on the registered signed instruction, on board approval, on who may hold equity and on the prohibition against pledging, stand as conditions in force.

## Points of judgement

A member on a class the catalogue does not allow a transfer on is not transferring, whatever instruction they sign. A member on an allowing class who names someone the class does not list is naming an ineligible transferee. A member on an allowing class naming a listed transferee, but with no signed instruction registered on the membership, has nothing on which equity may move. Membership and Patronage Equity carries all three conditions together, and each must hold.
